title: A smokeless flame
theme: The thumb-sized person is like a flame without smoke, the lord of what was and what will be; he is today and he is tomorrow. This is that.

words.meaning: of the measure of a thumb

words.context: Raṅgarāmānuja: like a fire of dry fuel, «शुष्केन्धनानलवत्»

words.meaning: of what has been and what will be

words.context: Śaṅkara: «इदानीं प्राणिषु वर्तमानः», present now in living beings
Śaṅkara: «श्वोऽपि वर्तिष्यते», will be tomorrow too

sandhi.type: s-stem before a vowel; a + a
sandhi.rule: The final s of jyotis becomes r before a vowel (P. 8.2.66 (ससजुषो रुँः)); a + a give ā, P. 6.1.101 (अकः सवर्णे दीर्घः).
-aḥ becomes -o before a voiced consonant, P. 6.1.114 (हशि च).

sandhi.type: saḥ before a vowel; a + a
sandhi.rule: The visarga of saḥ is lost before a vowel and the vowels stay apart; a + a give ā, P. 6.1.101 (अकः सवर्णे दीर्घः).
The visarga of saḥ is lost before a vowel, and the vowels stay apart.

samasa.vigraha: भूतं च भव्यं च तयोः समाहारः
samasa.meaning: what has been and what will be, together

morphology.note: a- ‘without’ + dhūma ‘smoke’ + the suffix -ka: ‘smokeless’. It is masculine, agreeing with puruṣaḥ, though it describes jyotiḥ, a neuter; Śaṅkara remarks that the neuter adhūmakam would be fitting, since it refers to the light: «अधूमकमिति युक्तं ज्योतिःपरत्वात्».

translation.literal: The person of the measure of a thumb [is] like a smokeless light, the ruler of what has been and will be; he alone [is] today, and he [is] tomorrow. This truly is that.
translation.readable: The person no bigger than a thumb is like a flame without smoke, lord of past and future. He is the same today and the same tomorrow. This is that.

anvaya: अङ्गुष्ठमात्रः पुरुषः अधूमकः ज्योतिः इव [अस्ति], भूतभव्यस्य ईशानः; सः एव अद्य, सः उ श्वः । एतत् वै तत् ।
syntax: Nominal sentences without a verb: puruṣaḥ … jyotir iva adhūmakaḥ, īśānaḥ; then two short clauses, sa evādya and sa u śvaḥ, with time-adverbs as predicates. The refrain closes the verse.

ambiguities.note: Śaṅkara: the same eternal, unchanging one is present now and will be tomorrow, and no other like him will be born, «नान्यस्तत्समोऽन्यश्च जनिष्यत इत्यर्थः»; Raṅgarāmānuja: the things of today and of tomorrow, of all three times, have him for their self, «कालत्रयवर्तिपदार्थ जातमपि तदात्मकमित्यर्थः».
Raṅgarāmānuja: shining like a fire of dry fuel, without smoke; Śaṅkara comments only on the gender of the word. The image suggests a light with nothing obscuring it.

metre.name: anuṣṭubh
metre.note: Counted as written, 15, 15 and 4 syllables. The second pāda, jyotir ivādhūmakaḥ, has seven, and eight if iva and adhūmakaḥ are kept apart, as GRETIL writes them (corrections.json); the fourth, sa evādya sa u śvaḥ, has seven, and eight with eva adya apart. The refrain etad vai tat (4) stands outside the metre.

beginner: The verse repeats the thumb-sized person of the last verse and adds two images. He is like a flame without smoke: pure light, with nothing clouding it. And he does not change with time: he is here today and will be the same tomorrow, the lord of all that was and all that will be. Śaṅkara takes this as a reply to the doubt Naciketas raised at the start, when he said some people think nothing remains after death; it also answers the view that everything lasts only a moment. Raṅgarāmānuja reads it a little differently: everything that exists today and everything that will exist tomorrow has this person for its inner self. The verse ends, like the others, with ‘this is that’.
analogy: Like a lamp burning clean oil in a still room: a steady flame with no smoke, the same light from one hour to the next.

commentary.label: direct
commentary.text: The thumb-sized person is like a smokeless flame, lord of past and future; he is the same today and tomorrow. This is that.

commentary.q: Śaṅkara: the same today and tomorrow
commentary.label: traditional
commentary.text: The one discerned in this way by yogins in the heart, «यस्त्वेवं लक्षितो योगिभिर्हृदये», the lord of past and future, is eternal and unchanging, «स एव नित्यः कूटस्थः»; present now in living beings, he will be so tomorrow; no other like him will be born. By its own words the scripture here answers the view ‘some say he is not’ (1.1.20), and the doctrine of momentariness too: «स्ववचनेन श्रुत्या प्रत्युक्तः, तथा क्षणभङ्गवादश्च».

commentary.q: Raṅgarāmānuja: the self of all times
commentary.label: traditional
commentary.text: Like a fire of dry fuel, «शुष्केन्धनानलवत्», he shines without smoke. ‘He is today, he is tomorrow’ means that all things of today and of tomorrow, «अद्यतनपदार्थजातं श्वस्तनपदार्थजातं», all things of the three times, have him for their self.

commentary.label: comparative
commentary.text: Madhva's passage filed under 2.1.12–14 concerns 2.1.14 only; in our source his bhāṣya says nothing on this verse.

commentary.q: The same words in the Bṛhadāraṇyaka
commentary.label: comparative
commentary.text: The Bṛhadāraṇyaka (1.5.23), which also has the sunrise line of 2.1.9, has the words «स एवाद्य स उ श्व» of prāṇa: the vow the gods made, kept today and tomorrow.

advaita.text: The self is eternal and unchanging, «स एव नित्यः कूटस्थः»; the verse refutes both the denial of the self after death and the doctrine of momentariness.

visistadvaita.text: Everything in the three times has the supreme Person for its self, «कालत्रयवर्तिपदार्थ जातमपि तदात्मकमित्यर्थः».

schools.disagreement: Śaṅkara reads ‘today and tomorrow’ as the unchanging persistence of the one self; Raṅgarāmānuja as the Person being the self of all things at every time. Madhva's bhāṣya has no comment on the verse in our source.

parallels.note: Śaṅkara quotes this verse, with the last, in deciding that the thumb-sized person is the supreme Self.
The same words in the Bṛhadāraṇyaka, said of prāṇa.
The doubt of Naciketas's third boon, which Śaṅkara says this verse answers.

contemporary.text: Moods, thoughts and circumstances change from one day to the next, yet something lets a person say ‘I’ of all of them. The verse points to that continuity and gives it the image of a steady, clear flame. This is a reflection, not a claim made by the text.

reflect.beginner: What in you was the same yesterday as it is today?
reflect.deeper: Śaṅkara hears in ‘he is today, he is tomorrow’ an answer to the doubt of 1.1.20. Why would that doubt need answering here, so late in the teaching?
reflect.practice: Light a candle or lamp and watch the flame for two minutes without doing anything else.

flags.note: ‘Today and tomorrow’: the unchanging persistence of the self (Śaṅkara) or the Person as the self of all things in time (Raṅgarāmānuja). Madhva's bhāṣya has no comment on the verse.
